name: Urumi
description: A flexible sword that acts like a whip.
cultural_significance: A highly dangerous weapon to both the wielder and opponent, mastered only by experienced Kalaripayattu warriors.

name: Khanda
cultural_significance: An iconic weapon of the Rajputs and Sikhs, symbolizing martial honor and divine justice.

name: Bagh Nakh
description: A claw-like weapon designed to fit over the knuckles or be concealed under and against the palm.
cultural_significance: Famously used by Shivaji Maharaj to defeat the Bijapur general Afzal Khan.

name: Gold Kahavanu
description: An ancient gold coin depicting a tiger, the royal emblem of the Cholas.
cultural_significance: Represents the vast economic power and trade network of the Chola empire.

name: Bronze Nataraja
description: A bronze sculpture depicting Shiva as the Lord of Dance.
cultural_significance: A masterpiece of Chola bronze casting, symbolizing the rhythmic cosmic cycle of creation and destruction.

name: Chola Bronze Shield
description: A sturdy circular shield adorned with the tiger emblem.
cultural_significance: Used by the elite Chola infantry and naval boarding parties.

name: Gold Varaha
description: A gold coin from the Vijayanagara empire, depicting a boar.
cultural_significance: The Varaha (boar avatar of Vishnu) was the royal emblem of the Vijayanagara emperors, and their standard currency.

name: Katar (Punch Dagger)
description: A type of push dagger characterized by its H-shaped horizontal hand grip.
cultural_significance: Unique to the Indian subcontinent, it became a symbol of status and martial prowess among Rajput nobles.

name: Silambam Staff
description: A smooth bamboo staff optimized for rapid strikes and blocks.
cultural_significance: The primary weapon of Silambam, teaching practitioners essential skills of distance management and fluid movement.

name: Decorated Gaja Tusk
description: An intricately carved ivory tusk representing war elephants.
cultural_significance: Elephants (Gaja) were a massive tactical asset and symbol of royal power for the Vijayanagara army.
